incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the victim of an elaborate AI-powered scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos depicting Leal offering fraudulent immigration services, including promises of US residency for $2,200. The scams escalated dramatically in recent months after potential clients began calling his office about services he never provided. Leal discovered fake accounts on TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram, with an anti-piracy company helping remove nearly 6,500 profiles across these platforms.

The scammers typically use social media videos to direct victims to contact numbers via WhatsApp, where they exchange emails and phony contracts before requesting payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Fake testimonials feature supposed clients praising Leal for obtaining legal status or securing releases from immigration detention. Leal warns immigrants to verify the identity of legal service providers and avoid those requesting immediate payment through digital payment apps. He has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the fraud.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
A fake online article featured a fabricated interview between ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler and Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock discussing Boulder Sparhaven, an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform. The article depicted an argument that never occurred. This type of scam is becoming increasingly common, with artificial intelligence making fraudulent content more convincing and difficult to detect. ASIC research reveals these schemes are growing more sophisticated, using deepfake images and videos of celebrities and politicians to promote illegitimate investments.

ASIC removed 19,400 scams last year, a 182 percent increase, including 5,476 phishing scams and 7,051 fake investment platforms. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Opposition Leader Angus Taylor, and finance presenter Alan Kohler are among the most commonly impersonated Australians, along with wealthy figures like Gina Rinehart and Dick Smith. Scammers build elaborate fake websites, news articles, and advertisements to deceive consumers. ASIC recommends verifying Australian Financial Services licence numbers through official registers before investing, while Kohler argues platforms distributing such content should face heavy fines.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
A lawsuit filed by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco accuses Oura, a smart ring company valued at eleven billion dollars, of false advertising regarding its sleep tracking capabilities. The suit seeks class action status and alleges that Oura's rings, which cost three hundred dollars and up, cannot accurately measure sleep stages as the company claims. According to the lawsuit, the devices rely on artificial intelligence generated guesses that are no more reliable than coin flips, rather than the physiological measurements that actual hospital sleep labs use with multiple electrodes.

The lawsuit challenges Oura's marketing claims, including statements about ninety-five percent sleep staging accuracy compared to clinical sleep labs. Oura responded by standing behind its science and research, stating that its rings use multiple physiological signals like heart rate and temperature. The company acknowledged that its rings are not medical devices or substitutes for clinical sleep studies, but said they have been validated in multiple peer reviewed studies. It remains unclear whether current Oura Ring customers will be able to join the suit or what compensation they might receive if the case proceeds to settlement or trial.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team identified the Aurora ransomware group operating since April 2026 with a Linux variant targeting ESXi environments. The group deployed a ransomware sample called encrypt.out that uses ChaCha20 encryption with RSA-4096 key wrapping. Attackers used a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to locate VMware ESXi hypervisors and vCenter servers on victim networks by scanning ports 443 and 902. Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators abused Cursor Agent running Claude Sonnet to conduct hands-on exploitation activities across ten target organizations, tasking the AI with installing VPN clients, scanning networks with Nmap, enumerating user privileges, and attempting NTLM relay attacks while maintaining strict operational restrictions.

Researchers identified a second Aurora cluster with medium confidence involving eight victim organizations across multiple countries. This cluster used different attack methods including exploiting SQL Server vulnerabilities and using GodPotato for privilege escalation before exfiltrating data to self-hosted S3 storage. The investigation revealed multiple command and control servers, proxy IPs, and the group's leak site at exposedrecords.io where stolen data appears nine days after exfiltration, confirming the connection between attack clusters.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
A Pizza Hut franchisee filed a lawsuit in Texas on May 6, claiming Pizza Hut's rollout of an AI-powered delivery system called Dragontail caused cascading operational problems and over $100 million in damages. Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the Northeast, alleges the system gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen workflows, allowing them to wait up to fifteen minutes to batch multiple orders together. This practice increased delivery times significantly and reduced customer satisfaction scores.

Before the 2024 rollout, Chaac achieved over 90% delivery times within thirty minutes and double-digit sales growth. After implementation, the company experienced sharp declines, with year-over-year sales in New York City dropping from positive 10.19% to negative 9.78%. The franchisee claims Pizza Hut failed to provide adequate training or support and ignored worsening metrics. Chaac seeks over $100 million in damages plus attorneys' fees, arguing Pizza Hut breached its franchise agreement. A Pizza Hut spokesperson said the company would respond through appropriate legal channels but declined further comment.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
Scammers have been sending personalized emails impersonating Terry Gross and other Fresh Air staff members to authors, entertainers and public figures, offering them interviews on the popular NPR program. The fraudulent messages include detailed references to the recipients' work and appear professionally legitimate, but eventually ask for money, typically around $250 for supposed production costs. Jennifer Black, a history professor at Misericordia University, received one such email and initially felt flattered until red flags emerged, including the request for payment and the unusual fact that Gross was personally handling logistics rather than production assistants.

According to cybersecurity experts, artificial intelligence has made these social engineering scams far more convincing and personalized than traditional mass-fraud attempts. Similar impersonation attempts have targeted comedians and journalists including Nikki Glaser, Amy Poehler and Katie Couric. WHYY, NPR and Fresh Air have stated they never charge guests for interviews and are working with law enforcement on the investigation. Experts advise potential victims to watch for red flags like payment requests and to verify interview invitations directly through official organization contacts rather than responding to suspicious emails.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
# Summary

A fake American think tank funded by the Israeli government published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days, designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots to generate pro-Israel arguments. The Hanover Institute for Public Policy, which does not exist as a legal entity, presented material on topics including Palestinian torture and Gaza aid shortages in a pseudo-academic format with carefully sourced citations. The site was built on a platform promising to optimize content for AI systems and was registered with the U.S. Justice Department as foreign agent material distributed for the Israeli government.

The operation represents part of a broader multimillion-dollar campaign financed by Israel and routed through European advertising firm Havas Media to manipulate AI training data and chatbot responses. Israeli officials have privately expressed frustration that despite spending tens of millions on public diplomacy efforts, American public support for Israel has declined significantly, with polling showing only 36 percent of Americans now sympathize with Israel. Experts warn the campaign demonstrates a new reality where foreign governments and others attempt to poison AI training data, making misinformation harder to fact-check.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels, including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, Capitol Records, and Atlantic Records, have filed separate lawsuits against Udio and Suno, two popular AI music generators. The labels accuse both companies of scraping massive amounts of copyrighted music without permission and using it to train their AI models. The lawsuits claim the companies have deliberately been evasive about their training data and argue that admitting what they copied would reveal willful copyright infringement on an enormous scale. The record labels submitted a lengthy list of thousands of copyrighted works they allege were scraped, featuring artists like The Beatles, Michael Jackson, Mariah Carey, Bruce Springsteen, and many others.

To support their claims, the record labels demonstrated they could recreate versions of famous copyrighted songs by using specific prompts in both AI generators. For example, prompting Suno with "1954 rock and roll billy haley comets" produced outputs copying Bill Haley's style and melody, and another prompt generated a song replicating Chuck Berry's "Johnny B. Goode." An Udio-generated song closely mimicked Green Day's "American Idiot" including its lyrics, while another nearly cloned Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You." The lawsuits set up a major court battle over how generative AI services should handle copyrighted material.

incidents.title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio
incidents.summary:
Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio by reaching licensing agreements. UMG had accused Udio of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence system, which creates original music from text prompts. The settlement includes plans for Udio to launch a new platform next year using only authorized and licensed music, allowing users to customize, stream and share their creations. UMG's CEO stated the agreements show their commitment to artists while embracing new technologies and developing new business models. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees, agreed that artists can participate in the new platform and receive compensation, though specifics remain undisclosed. This marks Udio's first major licensing deal with a record label. The lawsuit had claimed Udio created songs similar to hits like The Temptations' "My Girl" without permission. UMG also announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
State Farm's defense lawyers admitted to using artificial intelligence that generated fake legal cases, nonexistent quotes, and false legal holdings in court filings related to a Los Angeles homeowner's lawsuit. The homeowner, Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, sued State Farm and others after a 2020 fire made her Carson home uninhabitable, followed by water damage during repairs. She claimed delays in getting State Farm's approval prevented completion of reconstruction work, forcing her family to drain savings, declare bankruptcy, and lose the home to foreclosure. State Farm's attorney Jacquelene Robinson admitted using an AI tool called Irys and confirmed seven case citations across eight filings did not exist, along with incorrect case titles and misquoted passages.

Lead counsel Kenneth Katel accepted responsibility for the errors and stated the firm has updated its AI policies, though specifics were not provided. The discovery came after homeowner's attorney Eric Khodadian presented findings at an August 7 court hearing. A database of legal hallucinations worldwide has documented nearly 1,922 cases, predominantly in the United States, as AI use expands across the legal industry with 41 percent of law firms now using generative AI tools. The trial is scheduled for October.

stories.Headline: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia Extend Partnership in AI and Data
stories.Summary:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to deepen their cooperation in artificial intelligence, data governance, and emerging technologies. The agreement was announced following a meeting between Pakistan's Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja and Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority President Abdullah bin Sharaf Alghamdi at the LEAP 2026 conference in Riyadh. The two nations plan to establish a comprehensive and long-term technology partnership.

During the discussion, Pakistan's minister outlined the country's national AI and data governance initiatives while reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to building a strong data ecosystem and growing its digital economy. Both countries intend to collaborate on emerging technologies and create a lasting framework for cooperation. The partnership reflects a broader regional focus on advancing artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, technology skills, and data-driven development.

stories.Headline: Mark Cuban Foundation and Tonic Bring Free AI Bootcamp to Denver Teens
stories.Summary:
The Mark Cuban Foundation and Tonic are offering a free artificial intelligence bootcamp to high school students in Denver this fall. The program is open to ninth through twelfth graders and will run over three consecutive Saturdays on October 31, November 7, and November 14. All costs including meals, transportation, and technology will be covered for participants at no charge. Applications close on September 30.

The bootcamp provides hands-on experience with AI tools and explores real-world applications across fields like healthcare, business, sports science, and career preparation. Students will work on a capstone project guided by industry mentors. This Denver bootcamp is one of more than 35 similar programs being hosted across the United States by various companies. Mark Cuban emphasized the importance of providing AI education to underserved students to prepare them for future educational and employment opportunities.

stories.Summary:
Datametrex AI Limited announced plans to shut down its healthcare operations to focus on artificial intelligence, data centre technology, and patent licensing. The company operates medical clinics in Edmonton, Calgary, and Vancouver, British Columbia, providing primary and emergency care services. The gradual wind-down aims to streamline the corporate structure, reduce operating costs and regulatory requirements, and improve financial performance by redirecting resources toward core business areas.

The company will manage the transition carefully, considering operational, financial, contractual, and regulatory factors. Management plans to assess opportunities to maximize value from healthcare assets during the process. The strategic shift allows Datametrex to concentrate capital and resources on artificial intelligence and data centre initiatives, which align with long-term objectives. The company indicated it would provide further updates as developments occur.

stories.Headline: Oklahoma State University adds new AI, logistics programs for fall semester
stories.Summary:
Oklahoma State University Institute of Technology is launching two new academic programs beginning in fall 2026. The first is a 60-credit-hour online Associate in Applied Science in Logistics and Supply Chain Technology that students can complete in four to five semesters. This program covers warehousing, transportation, inventory management, and data-informed decision-making, preparing graduates for careers as logistics coordinators, distribution center managers, inventory specialists, and supply chain coordinators. The second offering is an Applied Artificial Intelligence option within the existing Bachelor of Technology in Information Technologies program.

The university designed both programs to address workforce demands in Oklahoma and beyond. The logistics program prepares students for industry-recognized credentials that can lead to over 11 million jobs nationwide. The artificial intelligence program goes beyond teaching tool usage, instead focusing on applying AI technologies to solve real organizational problems while considering ethics and governance. OSUIT Provost Dr. Richie Roberts stated that preparing students with skills aligned to industry needs helps build a strong workforce supporting the state's economic growth.

stories.Headline: Brazil's electoral court sets new standards for AI deepfakes after case involving Sen. Bolsonaro
stories.Summary:
Brazil's electoral court established new standards for identifying artificial intelligence-generated deepfakes in political advertising as the country prepares for October elections. The ruling came from a case involving opposition candidate Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who displayed AI-generated images of his imprisoned father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, at his party's convention in July. The court voted 4-3 to not punish Bolsonaro, determining the deepfake was used at a private event before his official candidacy announcement rather than as a public political advertisement.

In a separate 5-2 vote, the court defined political deepfakes as synthetic content created through artificial intelligence that realistically reproduces the image, voice, or speech of any person. These new standards will govern the vast amount of online campaign content from candidates leading up to the first round of voting on October 4. Broadcasters must allocate significant airtime for candidate advertisements, including 14 minutes daily for nearly 1,000 thirty-second ads.

stories.Headline: Protein Industries Canada invests in AI technology to boost on-farm productivity and bring new solutions to farmers
stories.Summary:
Protein Industries Canada is investing $4.9 million into two artificial intelligence projects designed to help Canadian farmers increase productivity and improve safety. The projects involve partnerships between companies like TerraVision360, Metos Canada, Rocky Mountain Equipment, Super GeoAI Technology Inc., and Southview Farms. The first project will create an AI tool to predict and manage disease risk in pulse crops by analyzing weather and crop data, enabling farmers to apply fungicides more strategically and reduce costs. The second project will develop a drone and LiDAR system to measure grain volumes in storage bins accurately while eliminating the need for dangerous manual climbing.

These investments are part of Canada's effort to advance agricultural innovation and support the adoption of made-in-Canada AI solutions. Government officials emphasized that the projects will strengthen farm competitiveness, reduce operational risks, and enhance worker safety across the agriculture sector. The funding comes through the Pan-Canadian Artificial Intelligence Strategy and supports the broader goal of growing Canada's plant-based food and ingredient industry to $25 billion.

stories.Headline: USF Faculty Split on AI Use in Classrooms
stories.Summary:
University of South Florida held a panel discussion Monday where faculty members debated whether artificial intelligence should be embraced, adapted to, or resisted in classroom settings. John Licato, an associate professor in the Bellini College of Artificial Intelligence, and Stephanie Arthur, an assistant professor in the College of Education, both support using AI tools. They argue that AI is already present in students' lives and can help with personalized learning and language support. Licato noted that AI can save students time and money on projects, while Arthur emphasized the importance of building AI literacy early, even starting with first graders.

Deepak Singh, a writing instructor at the Judy Genshaft Honors College, disagreed strongly. He believes AI undermines human creativity and intelligence, arguing that students should create work through their own effort rather than relying on machines. Singh also contends that students who learn without AI assistance retain more information. The faculty acknowledged that some concerns exist, including the potential for AI to replace meaningful human interaction and feedback necessary for learning.
